author: Jeff Hauser
title: Missouri's Eli Drinkwitz gives perfect response when Paul Finebaum asks about coaching rumors - NewsBreak
text:
By Jeff Hauser ,
1 hours ago
Missouri coach Eli Drinkwitz has been floated for several opening in college football as of late. So when he joined The Paul Finebaum Show on Wednesday, there was an expectation the topic would come up.
However, Drinkwitz didn't skip a beat when answering the inevitable question.
“It’s probably no more distracting than trying to decide if you’re going to run for United States Senate,” he said referencing reports that Finebaum might consider a political run. “There’s a lot of different things out there you’ve got to factor in.”
The gotcha statement by the Tigers coach was a perfectly timed zinger, “I'm supposed to be the expert in asking questions,” Finebaum said . “I’ll have to see if I can recover from that. I have to tell you, as somebody who has heard some great political answers that was the most atypical political answer I've ever heard. I mean, that was actually full of emotion and truth, which is why I think you should consider public office.”
After the laughs, Drinkwitz addressed the rumors head on.
“The reality is, we addressed it as a team, we addressed it as a staff,” Drinkwitz said. “All that stuff is fake right now. The only thing that matters is us playing Vanderbilt.”
No. 15 Missouri visits No. 10 Vanderbilt on Saturday in a matchup that will draw ESPN’s College GameDay to Nashville. Drinkwitz downplayed the spotlight, saying his team is focused solely on the field.
He ended the interview with a final jab, which threw the hot potato right back at Finebaum.
“This football team, these boosters, these fans — they put a whole lot into us being focused on the right here, right now,” he said. “And whether or not you run for Senate, that’s up to you.”
